issues.legal_issue: When no date is fixed for performance of an agreement for sale, limitation for specific performance depends on when the plaintiff had notice that performance was refused, and ordinarily cannot be decided as a preliminary issue without evidence.
material_facts: The agreement for sale fixed no date for performance.
The plaintiffs alleged that they learned of the defendants’ refusal when the defendants objected to a proposed purchase, and they filed suit within six months of that objection.
The defendants disputed the plaintiffs’ account, and the courts below decided limitation without taking evidence on when the plaintiffs had notice of refusal.
issues.conclusion: The finding that the specific-performance claim was barred by limitation was set aside. The limitation issue must be decided after the parties have an opportunity to adduce evidence; the Court did not itself determine that the claim was timely.
issues.legal_principle: Article 54 of the Limitation Act, 1963 has two limbs. If the agreement fixes a time for performance, limitation runs from that time; if it does not, limitation runs from when the plaintiff has notice that performance is refused. Under Section 3, a suit filed beyond the prescribed period must be dismissed, but where the second limb of Article 54 applies, the date of notice will ordinarily require evidence. The Court relied on R.K. Parvatharaj Gupta v. K.C. Jayadeva Reddy and held that a preliminary decision may be appropriate where the plaint admits notice of refusal more than three years before suit, which was not the case here.

rule.if: specific_performance_suit and no_performance_date_fixed and refusal_notice_not_admitted_to_be_over_three_years_old and limitation_decided_without_trial_evidence

predicates.specific_performance_suit: The plaintiff brought a suit seeking specific performance of an agreement for sale.
predicates.no_performance_date_fixed: The agreement did not fix a date for its performance.
predicates.refusal_notice_not_admitted_to_be_over_t: The plaintiff did not admit that notice of refusal occurred more than three years before filing suit.
predicates.limitation_decided_without_trial_evidenc: The court decided limitation without receiving evidence about when the plaintiff had notice of refusal.

issues.definition: When a specific-performance suit concerns an agreement with no fixed performance date and the timing of notice of refusal is not admitted to be outside the limitation period, a decision on limitation without evidence must be set aside and the issue decided after evidence.

issues.legal_issue: A claim for an injunction protecting alleged possession cannot be dismissed as time-barred merely because the related claim for specific performance is found time-barred.
material_facts: The suit sought both specific performance and a perpetual injunction against interference with the plaintiffs’ alleged possession.
The plaintiffs alleged that their predecessor had been put in possession under a subsequent agreement or receipt.

The courts below dismissed the suit as a whole based on their finding that the specific-performance claim was time-barred, without determining the limitation period applicable to the injunction claim.
issues.conclusion: The injunction claim could not be held barred at the preliminary stage on the basis of the limitation finding concerning specific performance. Its limitation and whether it was independent or consequential required determination on the pleadings and evidence.
issues.legal_principle: A claim for injunction is governed by Article 113 of the Limitation Act, 1963, and its limitation period depends on when the right to sue accrued. Whether an injunction is independent of, or merely consequential to, a claim for specific performance and whether the plaintiff proves possession are matters for determination on the pleadings and evidence. Section 27 of the Limitation Act concerns extinguishment of a right to property at the end of the period for a suit for possession; the Court noted that the suit was not, as such, a suit for possession.

predicates.suit_includes_possession_protection_inju: The plaintiff sought an injunction to protect alleged possession of the property.
predicates.specific_performance_claim_dismissed_as_: The court dismissed the specific-performance claim as time-barred.
predicates.injunction_limitation_not_separately_det: The court did not separately determine when the right to sue for the injunction accrued.

issues.definition: When a suit includes an injunction to protect alleged possession, a time-bar finding on the specific-performance claim does not dispose of the injunction claim if its own limitation period has not been determined.

issues.legal_issue: Delay and the time reasonably allowed for performance may bear on entitlement to discretionary specific performance, but they cannot, without the required limitation finding, support preliminary dismissal as time-barred.
material_facts: The suit was filed many years after the agreement for sale.
The agreement fixed no date for performance, and the parties disputed payment, performance of the vendors’ obligations, delivery of possession, and the plaintiffs’ readiness and willingness.
The courts below dismissed the suit on limitation without a trial.
issues.conclusion: The effects of delay, the reasonable time for performance, and the plaintiffs’ entitlement to discretionary specific performance must be considered after evidence; they could not support dismissal of the suit as time-barred at the preliminary stage.
issues.legal_principle: Section 46 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872 requires performance within a reasonable time where no time is specified, with reasonableness depending on the circumstances. The Court also referred to Section 20 of the Specific Relief Act and the discretionary nature of specific performance. Those matters, including readiness and willingness and the effect of delay, are distinct from determining limitation under Article 54 of the Limitation Act, 1963 and require consideration on the evidence.

rule.if: specific_performance_suit and no_performance_date_fixed and substantial_delay_alleged and material_performance_facts_require_evidence

predicates.specific_performance_suit: The plaintiff brought a suit seeking specific performance of an agreement for sale.
predicates.no_performance_date_fixed: The agreement did not specify a time for performance.
predicates.substantial_delay_alleged: A party relied on the long interval between the agreement and the suit.
predicates.material_performance_facts_require_evide: Material facts about performance, readiness and willingness, or the parties’ obligations remained disputed and unproved.

issues.definition: When a specific-performance suit involves an agreement without a fixed performance date, alleged substantial delay, and disputed material facts, delay and reasonable time must be assessed after evidence rather than used as a preliminary limitation bar.
